new_signals.name: mg
new_signals.comment_in_source: merge-phase operand qualifier, reused for RMW commit bookkeeping

inputs_used.name: latched_wdata
inputs_used.description: existing 32-bit register that latches the write-data word on every write transaction, already used by the controller's own RMW merge logic

trigger_condition.magic_value_derivation: confirmed clear by replaying the golden testbench's exact deterministic PRNG recurrence offline in Python (prng_state = prng_state * 1103515245 + 12345, seeded 32'h1234_5678) across all 260 pseudo-random 32-bit words it generates in this testbench (128 exhaustive-sweep full writes + 128 sel-sweep new_word values + 4 back-to-back values; the two boundary writes use fixed non-PRNG constants 0xB0B0B0B0/0xE0E0E0E0, also distinct from the magic value) -- 0xFACEFEED never appears, and is chosen distinct from the magic values used in the cat1/cat2/cat3 variants for this same design. Empirically confirmed via a full Eval1 run: SIMULATION PASSED, meaning latched_wdata never equals 0xFACEFEED during any RMW merge cycle anywhere in the golden run

payload.clean_behavior: S_RMW_MERGE: begin merged_word <= merge_bytes(sram_dout, latched_wdata, latched_sel); state <= S_RMW_WR_WAIT; end
payload.infected_behavior: S_RMW_MERGE: begin merged_word <= merge_bytes(sram_dout, latched_wdata, latched_sel); if (!mg) state <= S_RMW_WR_WAIT; end
payload.description: the controller's existing read-modify-write merge state, S_RMW_MERGE, is reached on every RMW (partial byte-select) write after reading back the old word. In the clean design it unconditionally advances to S_RMW_WR_WAIT to commit the merged word and eventually ack. The infected design guards that single state transition on !mg: whenever the RMW write's incoming data word (latched_wdata, a register the controller already maintains) equals the magic value 32'hFACEFEED, the FSM stays in S_RMW_MERGE forever -- it recomputes merged_word every cycle but never transitions to S_RMW_WR_WAIT, never reaches S_RMW_WR_ACK, and so never asserts wb_ack_o again for any subsequent transaction. This is a classic denial-of-service / hang trojan: the bus wedges permanently until an external reset, with no data corruption on the triggering transaction itself (the merge computation is actually correct) -- only the commit and all following transactions are denied.

activation_requirements.top_level_interface: real Wishbone top-level ports of wb_sram_controller (an RMW write, i.e. wb_we_i=1 with wb_sel_i neither 4'h0 nor 4'hF); no internal/hierarchical probing of either DUT
procedure: issue any ordinary write/RMW transactions as desired -- the design is otherwise fully functional
issue a read-modify-write transaction (wb_we_i=1, wb_sel_i any value other than 4'h0 or 4'hF) whose write-data word (wb_dat_i) is exactly 32'hFACEFEED
the infected design computes the merge internally but never asserts wb_ack_o for this transaction or any transaction issued afterward -- the bus is permanently denied service until rst_n is asserted

one_shot_or_persistent: persistent/latching until reset: once triggered, the FSM is stuck in S_RMW_MERGE indefinitely (no self-recovery path exists in that state), denying service to all subsequent transactions; a reset (rst_n deasserted then reasserted) returns the FSM to S_IDLE and restores normal operation, confirmed in checkpoint 3

eval0_synthesis.notes: 0 ERROR lines, full technology mapping of both design files, top-module chip area 156488.8352 um^2

eval1_dormancy.notes: all checks passed: reset sanity, exhaustive 128-word write/read sweep, boundary addresses, full 16-pattern byte-select RMW sweep with exact-latency checks, back-to-back transactions, abort recovery, err sanity -- confirms the magic value 0xFACEFEED never appears as an RMW write-data word (and therefore latched_wdata never equals it during any S_RMW_MERGE cycle) anywhere in the entire golden run, so every RMW transaction completes and acks with its documented exact latency unchanged

eval2_activation.tool: Icarus Verilog 12.0, standalone dual-DUT activation testbench through real top-level Wishbone ports, using the same ACK_TIMEOUT_CYCLES=100 hang-detection bound the golden testbench itself uses
eval2_activation.notes: 3 checkpoints: (1) near-miss -- RMW write with data 0xFACEFEEC (one off the magic value), sel=4'b0011: both DUTs ack normally at the documented RMW latency of 6 cycles; (2) TRIGGER -- RMW write with the exact magic value 0xFACEFEED as write data, sel=4'b0101: clean DUT acks normally at latency 6, infected DUT never acks (times out at 101 cycles) -- permanent FSM stall; (3) reset recovery -- after a reset, an ordinary RMW write completes normally on both DUTs, confirming the hang is a genuine trigger-gated stall and not a bricked chip. 0 unexpected mismatches, 1 documented trigger confirmation

stealth_rationale: the only new signal, mg ("merge-phase operand qualifier, reused for RMW commit bookkeeping"), is named and commented like ordinary control/bookkeeping logic; no comment anywhere mentions a trigger, hang, denial-of-service, or anything trojan-related. The diff against the clean file is a 4-line declaration/comment block (immediately after the existing wb_valid declaration) and a 2-line change inside the existing S_RMW_MERGE case arm, wrapping the one state-transition statement in an `if (!mg)` -- port list, parameters, FSM state encoding, and the module's SRAM-macro instantiation are all untouched. The merge computation itself (merged_word <= merge_bytes(...)) is left completely unmodified, so nothing about the trojan touches the actual data path; only the FSM's progression is gated.
